metadata.title: A Note on Spectral Analysis in automorphic representation theory for $\GL_2$: II

extraction_notes.note: Theorem 2.11 is titled an adelic version of regularization due to Zagier [Za82] (adelic setting first in [MV10]); kept origin external although part (4) adds the degenerate term and the paper proves it.
Theorems 3.4 and 3.7 are proved by prose computations placed before their statements that establish only part (2) resp. (3); the other parts get no proof, so both theorems carry rigor semi_formal.

Theorem 3.4 opens with an unfinished sentence ('If ... is spherical, we also write'); Proposition 2.20 is announced as a fact 'of which we omit the proof' but a proof follows. Appendix text cites 'Section 4.2/4.4' for what are Sections 5.2/5.4.

The introduction's three informal definitions (1)-(3) of the regularized integral and the suggested convention that the regularized integral of E^reg(1/2,e_0) is 0 are motivation, not used later; left out.

nodes.name: Regularizable function on R_+
nodes.statement: Let $a: \ag{R}_+ \to \ag{C}$ be a continuous function. It is \emph{regularizable} if \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] for any $N \gg 1$ as $t \to \infty$ $$ a(t) = f(t)+O(t^{-N}), \quad f(t)=\sum_{i=1}^l \frac{c_i}{n_i!} t^{\frac{1}{2}+\alpha_i} \log^{n_i}t, $$ where $c_i, \alpha_i \in \ag{C}, n_i \in \ag{N}$; \item[(2)] for some $\alpha \in \ag{R}$ as $t \to 0^+$ $$ a(t) = O(t^{\alpha}). $$ \end{itemize} In this case, we write for $T > 0$ $$ h_T(s) = \sum_{i=1}^l \frac{c_i}{n_i!} \frac{\partial^{n_i}}{\partial s^{n_i}} \left( \frac{T^{s+\alpha_i}}{s+\alpha_i} \right) = \sum_{i=1}^l c_i \sum_{m=0}^{n_i} \frac{(-1)^{n_i-m}}{m!} \frac{T^{s+\alpha_i} \log^m T}{(s+\alpha_i)^{n_i-m+1}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: $a$ on $\mathbb{R}_+$ is regularizable if it has a finite asymptotic expansion in $t^{1/2+\alpha_i}\log^{n_i}t$ at $\infty$ and polynomial bound at $0$; defines $h_T(s)$.
nodes.label: RegFuncRDef

nodes.name: Integrability forces exponent bound
nodes.statement: For $f(t)$ as above, if $\lim_{T \to \infty} \int_1^T f(t) \frac{dt}{t^2}$ exists, then $\Re \alpha_i < 1/2$ for all $1 \leq i \leq l$.
conclusions: $\Re \alpha_i < 1/2$ for all $1 \leq i \leq l$
nodes.statement_short: If $\int_1^\infty f(t)\,dt/t^2$ converges, all exponents satisfy $\Re\alpha_i<1/2$.
nodes.label: IntExpBd

nodes.name: Circle group T
nodes.statement: Write $\ag{T} = \ag{R} / \ag{Z}$.

nodes.name: Frequency vector theta
nodes.statement: Let $\vec{\theta} = (\theta_1, \cdots, \theta_n) \in \ag{R}^n$.

nodes.name: Image [x] in the torus
nodes.statement: For any $\vec{x} \in \ag{R}^n$, we write by $[\vec{x}]$ its image in $\ag{T}^n$.

nodes.name: Subtorus T_theta
nodes.statement:
Define
	$$ \ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}} = \overline{\lbrace [t\vec{\theta}] : t\in \ag{R} \rbrace}. $$

nodes.name: T_theta is a closed subgroup
nodes.statement: It is a closed subgroup of $\ag{T}^n$.

nodes.name: Unique ergodicity of the one-parameter subgroup
nodes.statement: Furthermore, the one parameter subgroup $U_{\vec{\theta}} = \lbrace t.\vec{\theta} : t \in \ag{R} \rbrace$ of $\ag{R}^n$ acts uniquely ergodically on $\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}}$ w.r.t. the Haar measure of $\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}}$.

nodes.name: Unique ergodicity of linear flow on a subtorus
nodes.statement: For any $f \in {\rm C}(\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}})$, we have $$ \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T}\int_0^T f([\vec{x}] + [t.\vec{\theta}]) dt = \int_{\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}}} f dm_{\theta} $$ for all $[\vec{x}] \in \ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}}$. Here $dm_{\theta}$ is the normalized Haar measure on $\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}}$.
conclusions: $$ \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T}\int_0^T f([\vec{x}] + [t.\vec{\theta}]) dt = \int_{\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}}} f dm_{\theta} $$ for all $[\vec{x}] \in \ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}}$
nodes.statement_short: Time averages of continuous functions along the flow $t\vec\theta$ on $\mathbb{T}_{\vec\theta}$ converge to the Haar integral.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3

Consider the group of characters ${m Ch}(\ag{T}^n)$ of $\ag{T}^n$ given by $$ e_{\vec{n}}(\vec{x}) = e(\vec{n} \cdot \vec{x}) = e(\sum_{i=1}^n n_i x_i), \vec{n} \in \ag{N}^n, \vec{x} \in \ag{R}^n $$ where $e(x) = e^{2\pi i x}$. By the duality theorem for locally compact abelian groups, the group of characters ${m Ch}(\ag{T}_{\vec{	heta}})$ is the quotient of ${m Ch}(\ag{T}^n)$ by the subgroup of $e_{\vec{n}}$'s which vanish on $\ag{T}_{\vec{	heta}}$. Obviously, we have $$ e_{\vec{n}}(\ag{T}_{\vec{	heta}})=1 \Leftrightarrow e(t\vec{n} \cdot \vec{	heta}) = 1 	ext{ for }  orall t \in \ag{R} \Leftrightarrow \vec{n} \cdot \vec{	heta}=0. $$ So ${m Ch}(\ag{T}_{\vec{	heta}})$ are $e_{\vec{n}}$'s modulo the subgroup of $e_{\vec{n}}$'s with $\vec{n} \cdot \vec{	heta}=0$. Let $[e_{\vec{n}}] 
eq 0$ denote a non trivial equivalence class of $e_{\vec{n}}$ in the quotient group, we calculate $$ \extnorm{  rac{1}{T} \int_0^T [e_{\vec{n}}]( [\vec{x}] + [t\vec{	heta}] ) dt } = \extnorm{  rac{e(\vec{n} \cdot \vec{x})}{T} \cdot  rac{e(T\vec{n} \cdot \vec{	heta} ) - 1}{\vec{n} \cdot \vec{	heta}} } \leq  rac{2}{
orm[T] \cdot 
orm[\vec{n} \cdot \vec{	heta}]} 	o 0, T 	o \infty. $$ The lemma is thus proved for $f = [e_{\vec{n}}]$, hence the $\ag{C}$-vector space generated by ${m Ch}(\ag{T}_{\vec{	heta}})$, which is also a $*$-subalgebra of ${m C}(\ag{T}_{\vec{	heta}})$. The lemma then follows by a standard application of the complex version of the Stone-Weierstrass theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Check the limit on characters of $\mathbb{T}_{\vec\theta}$ by direct integration, then extend by Stone-Weierstrass.

nodes.name: Limits of almost periodic sums are constant
nodes.statement: Consider the function $f(x) = \sum_{k=1}^n a_k x^{i \theta_k}, x \in \ag{R}_+$, where $a_k \in \ag{C}, \theta_k \in \ag{R}, 1\leq k \leq n$. If $\lim_{x \to +\infty} f(x)$ exists, then $f(x)$ is a constant function.
assumptions: $f(x) = \sum_{k=1}^n a_k x^{i \theta_k}, x \in \ag{R}_+$, where $a_k \in \ag{C}, \theta_k \in \ag{R}, 1\leq k \leq n$
conclusions: $f(x)$ is a constant function
nodes.statement_short: A finite sum $\sum a_k x^{i\theta_k}$ with a limit at $+\infty$ is constant.
nodes.label: ErgodicLemma

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.4
nodes.statement: Note that $f(e^{2\pi t}) = \sum_{k=1}^n a_k e(t\theta_k), t \in \ag{R}$. If $f$ is not constant, we can find $t_1, t_2 \in \ag{R}$ s.t. $f(e^{2\pi t_1}) \neq f(e^{2\pi t_2})$. By continuity, we then find some neighborhood $U_1$ of $[t_1 \vec{\theta}]$, and $U_2$ of $[t_2 \vec{\theta}]$ such that $$ \sum_{k=1}^n a_k e(x_k) \neq \sum_{k=1}^n a_k e(y_k), \forall \vec{x} \in U_1, \vec{y} \in U_2. $$ But the flow $\gamma(t) = [t\vec{\theta}]$ meets both $U_1$ and $U_2$ infinitely often by the lemma, hence $\lim_{t \to \infty} f(e^{2\pi t})$ can not exist, contradicting the hypothesis.
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction: a non-constant $f$ separates two open sets that the flow visits infinitely often by Lemma 2.3.

nodes.name: Slowly increasing function
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi: {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})\gp{Z}(\ag{A}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}) \to \ag{C}$ be a continuous function. It is \emph{slowly increasing} if for some $c \in \ag{R}$ and $g$ lying in some Siegel domain we have $$ \norm[\varphi(g)] \ll {\rm Ht}(g)^c, {\rm Ht}(g) \to \infty. $$
differentia: for some $c \in \ag{R}$ and $g$ lying in some Siegel domain we have $$ \norm[\varphi(g)] \ll {\rm Ht}(g)^c, {\rm Ht}(g) \to \infty. $$
nodes.label: SlowIncDef

nodes.name: Regularizing kernel
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi: {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})\gp{Z}(\ag{A}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}) \to \ag{C}$ be a slowly increasing function. Its \emph{regularizing kernel} $a(t,\varphi)$ is $$ a(t,\varphi) = \int_{\mathbf{F} \backslash \ag{A} \times \mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{(1)} \times \gp{K}} \varphi(n(x)a(t^+y)k) dx d^{\times}y dk, $$ where $t^+ = s_{\mathbf{F}}(t)$ is the image of $t$ under the section of the adelic norm map $\ag{A}^{\times} \to \ag{R}_+$ recalled in the beginning of this paper.
nodes.statement_short: $a(t,\varphi)$ is the integral of $\varphi(n(x)a(t^+y)k)$ over $x$, norm-one ideles $y$ and $k\in K$ (constant term along the height).

nodes.name: Regularizable function on PGL_2
nodes.statement: We call a slowly increasing function $\varphi: {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})\gp{Z}(\ag{A}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}) \to \ag{C}$ \emph{regularizable} if its regularizing kernel $a(t,\varphi)$ satisfies the condition (1) of Definition \ref{RegFuncRDef}. In this case, we define for $s \in \ag{C}, \Re s \gg 1$ $$ R(s,\varphi) = \int_0^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t)) t^{s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t}; \quad R^*(s,\varphi) = \Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s) R(s,\varphi). $$ The space of regularizable functions is denoted by $\mathcal{A}^{{\rm reg}}({\rm GL}_2)$.
differentia: its regularizing kernel $a(t,\varphi)$ satisfies the condition (1) of Definition \ref{RegFuncRDef}
nodes.statement_short: Slowly increasing $\varphi$ is regularizable if its regularizing kernel is; defines the Mellin-type transform $R(s,\varphi)$ and $R^*$.
nodes.label: RegFuncDef

nodes.name: Condition at zero is automatic
nodes.statement: This is equivalent to saying $a(t,\varphi)$ regularizable, i.e., the condition (2) of Definition \ref{RegFuncRDef} is automatically satisfied due to the following Corollary \ref{SIncBdAt0}.

nodes.name: Height bound off the Borel
nodes.statement: If $\gamma \in {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F}) - \gp{B}(\mathbf{F})$, then we have $ {\rm Ht}(\gamma g) \leq {\rm Ht}(g)^{-1}$.
conclusions: $ {\rm Ht}(\gamma g) \leq {\rm Ht}(g)^{-1}$
nodes.label: HtBd

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.9
nodes.statement: This is \cite[Lemma 3.19]{Wu5}.
nodes.statement_short: Cited from [Wu5, Lemma 3.19].

nodes.name: Bound of slowly increasing functions near height zero
nodes.statement: If $\varphi$ is slowly increasing as in Definition \ref{SlowIncDef}, then we have $$ \norm[\varphi(g)] \ll {\rm Ht}(g)^{\min(0,-c)}, {\rm Ht}(g) \to 0. $$
assumptions: $\varphi$ is slowly increasing as in Definition \ref{SlowIncDef}
conclusions: $$ \norm[\varphi(g)] \ll {\rm Ht}(g)^{\min(0,-c)}, {\rm Ht}(g) \to 0. $$
nodes.label: SIncBdAt0

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.10
nodes.statement:
If $c \leq 0$, then it is easy to see that $\varphi$ is bounded, since elements of bounded height in a Siegel domain form a compact subset and $\varphi$ is continuous. The same argument shows that if $c<0$ we can assume $
orm[\varphi(g)] \ll {m Ht}(g)^c$ to hold in a whole Siegel domain $S$ containing a fundamental domain. If ${m Ht}(g)$ is small, we take $\gamma \in {m GL}_2(\mathbf{F})$ such that $\gamma g \in S$, thus by the lemma we get $$ 
orm[\varphi(g)] = 
orm[\varphi(\gamma g)] \ll {m Ht}(\gamma g)^c \leq {m Ht}(g)^{-c}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Bounded if $c\le 0$; otherwise move $g$ into a Siegel domain by $\gamma$ and apply the height bound of Lemma 2.9.

nodes.name: Function lambda_F(s)
nodes.statement: \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s) := \frac{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(-2s)}{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(2+2s)} = \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{-1}(0)}{s} + \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{s^n}{n!} \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(n)}(0).
nodes.statement_short: Defines $\lambda_{\mathbf F}(s)=\Lambda_{\mathbf F}(-2s)/\Lambda_{\mathbf F}(2+2s)$ and its Laurent expansion at $0$.
nodes.label: lambdaFDef

nodes.name: Truncation operator
nodes.statement: Recall the truncation operator $\Lambda^c$ defined in \cite[(5.5)]{GJ79}.

nodes.name: Spherical section f_0
nodes.statement: Let $f_0 \in {\rm Ind}_{\gp{B}(\ag{A}) \cap \gp{K}}^{\gp{K}} (1,1)$ be constant equal to $1$ on $\gp{K}$.

nodes.name: Adelic version of Zagier's regularization
nodes.statement: (Adelic version of regularization due to Zagier \cite{Za82}) \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] Let $\varphi: {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})\gp{Z}(\ag{A}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}) \to \ag{C}$ be a slowly increasing function. For $s \in \ag{C}, \Re s \gg 1$ and any $T \gg 1$ we have $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi(g) \Lambda^T {\rm E}(s,f_0)(g) dg = \int_0^T a(t,\varphi)t^{s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t} - \int_T^{\infty} a(t,\varphi) t^{-s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t} \cdot \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s-1/2). $$ \item[(2)] If $\varphi$ is, in addition, regularizable, then we have for $T \gg 1$ \begin{align*} &\quad R^*(s,\varphi) + \Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s) h_T(s) + \Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1-2s) h_T(-s) \\ &= \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi(g) \Lambda^T {\rm E}^*(s,f_0)(g) dg + \\ &\quad \Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s) \int_T^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t)) t^{s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t} + \Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1-2s) \int_T^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t)) t^{-s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t}. \end{align*} In particular, $R(s,\varphi)$ has a meromorphic continuation to $s \in \ag{C}$ with possible poles at $s=\pm 1/2, \pm \alpha_i, (\rho-1)/2$ for $\rho$ running over the non-trivial zeros of $\zeta_{\mathbf{F}}$, and satisfies the functional equation $$ R^*(s,\varphi) = R^*(-s,\varphi). $$ \item[(3)] Under the condition of (2), if $\Re \alpha_i < 0$ for all $1 \leq i \leq l$, then we have $$ R(s,\varphi) = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi(g) {\rm E}(s,f_0)(g) dg, \quad \max_{1 \leq i \leq l} \alpha_i < \Re s < -\max_{1 \leq i \leq l} \alpha_i. $$ \item[(4)] Under the condition of (2), if $\varphi$ is integrable on $ [{\rm PGL}_2] := {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})\gp{Z}(\ag{A}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}) $, then we have $\Re \alpha_i < 1/2$ for all $1 \leq i \leq l$, and $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi(g) dg = \frac{1}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} \left( {\rm Res}_{s=\frac{1}{2}} R(s,\varphi) + c_i \delta_{\substack{\alpha_i=-\frac{1}{2} \\ n_i=0}} \right), \quad {\rm Vol}([{\rm PGL}_2]) = \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0). $$ \end{itemize}

assumptions: Let $\varphi: {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})\gp{Z}(\ag{A}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}) \to \ag{C}$ be a slowly increasing function.
conclusions: $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi(g) \Lambda^T {\rm E}(s,f_0)(g) dg = \int_0^T a(t,\varphi)t^{s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t} - \int_T^{\infty} a(t,\varphi) t^{-s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t} \cdot \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s-1/2). $$

In particular, $R(s,\varphi)$ has a meromorphic continuation to $s \in \ag{C}$ with possible poles at $s=\pm 1/2, \pm \alpha_i, (\rho-1)/2$ for $\rho$ running over the non-trivial zeros of $\zeta_{\mathbf{F}}$, and satisfies the functional equation $$ R^*(s,\varphi) = R^*(-s,\varphi). $$
$$ R(s,\varphi) = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi(g) {\rm E}(s,f_0)(g) dg, \quad \max_{1 \leq i \leq l} \alpha_i < \Re s < -\max_{1 \leq i \leq l} \alpha_i. $$

assumptions: if $\varphi$ is integrable on $ [{\rm PGL}_2] := {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})\gp{Z}(\ag{A}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}) $
conclusions: we have $\Re \alpha_i < 1/2$ for all $1 \leq i \leq l$

assumptions: Let $\varphi: {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})\gp{Z}(\ag{A}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}) \to \ag{C}$ be a slowly increasing function.
if $\varphi$ is integrable on $ [{\rm PGL}_2] := {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})\gp{Z}(\ag{A}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}) $
conclusions: $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi(g) \Lambda^T {\rm E}(s,f_0)(g) dg = \int_0^T a(t,\varphi)t^{s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t} - \int_T^{\infty} a(t,\varphi) t^{-s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t} \cdot \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s-1/2). $$

In particular, $R(s,\varphi)$ has a meromorphic continuation to $s \in \ag{C}$ with possible poles at $s=\pm 1/2, \pm \alpha_i, (\rho-1)/2$ for $\rho$ running over the non-trivial zeros of $\zeta_{\mathbf{F}}$, and satisfies the functional equation $$ R^*(s,\varphi) = R^*(-s,\varphi). $$
$$ R(s,\varphi) = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi(g) {\rm E}(s,f_0)(g) dg, \quad \max_{1 \leq i \leq l} \alpha_i < \Re s < -\max_{1 \leq i \leq l} \alpha_i. $$
we have $\Re \alpha_i < 1/2$ for all $1 \leq i \leq l$
nodes.statement_short: Rankin-Selberg unfolding against truncated $E(s,f_0)$: meromorphic continuation and functional equation of $R(s,\varphi)$, and the integral of an integrable $\varphi$ as a residue at $s=1/2$.
nodes.label: AdelicRegThm

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.11
nodes.statement:
Since the proofs of (1) to (3) are quite similar to that in \cite{Za82}, we only mention some essential points of them. Only (4) needs more explanation. 
oindent (1) This is standard Rankin-Selberg unfolding together with $$ \Lambda^T {m E}(s,f_0)(g) = \sum_{\gamma \in \gp{B}(\mathbf{F})  ackslash {m GL}_2(\mathbf{F})} f_{0,s}(\gamma g) 1_{{m Ht}(\gamma g) \leq T} - \sum_{\gamma \in \gp{B}(\mathbf{F})  ackslash {m GL}_2(\mathbf{F})} \mathcal{M} f_{0,s}(\gamma g) 1_{{m Ht}(\gamma g) > T}. $$ 
oindent (2) It follows from rewriting the two terms at the right hand side of (1). For the first term we have  egin{align*} \int_0^T a(t,\varphi) t^{s- rac{1}{2}}  rac{dt}{t} &= R(s,\varphi) - \int_T^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t)) t^{s- rac{1}{2}}  rac{dt}{t} + \sum_{i=1}^l  rac{c_i}{n_i!} \int_0^T t^{s+\alpha_i} \log^{n_i} t  rac{dt}{t} \ &= R(s,\varphi) - \int_T^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t)) t^{s- rac{1}{2}}  rac{dt}{t} + h_T(s). \end{align*} For the second term we have a similar equality. 
oindent (3) In the case $\Re \alpha_i < 0$ for all $i$, we let $T 	o \infty$, taking into account Proposition ef{GlobRDEisWhi} and $h_T(s) 	o 0$, to get the asserted equation. 
oindent (4) The integrability of $\varphi$ implies $\Re \alpha_i < 1/2$ for all $i$ by Lemma ef{IntExpBd}. We take residue at $s=1/2$ on both sides of the equation obtained in (2) and divide by $\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s)$ to see for $T \gg 1$  egin{align*} &\quad {m Res}_{s= rac{1}{2}} R(s,\varphi) + {m Res}_{s= rac{1}{2}} h_T(s) + \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0) h_T(- rac{1}{2}) \ &= \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0) \int_{\mathcal{D}_T} \varphi(g)dg + {m Res}_{s= rac{1}{2}} \int_{\mathcal{D}-\mathcal{D}_T} \varphi(g) \left( {m E}(s,f_0)(g) - {m E}(s,f_0)_N(g) ight) dg \ &\quad + \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0) \int_T^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t))  rac{dt}{t^2}, \end{align*} where $\mathcal{D}$ is the standard fundamental domain for $[{m PGL}_2]$ and $\mathcal{D}_T$ is the set of $g \in \mathcal{D}$ such that ${m Ht}(g) \leq T$. It is easy to see that as $T 	o \infty$ $$ h_T(- rac{1}{2}) 	o 0; \quad \int_T^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t))  rac{dt}{t^2} 	o 0. $$ By Proposition ef{GlobRDEisWhi}, ${m E}(s,f_0)(g) - {m E}(s,f_0)_N(g)$ is of uniformly rapid decay with respect to ${m Ht}(g), g \in \mathcal{D}$ as $s$ remains in a compact neighborhood of $1/2$. Hence $$ \int_{\mathcal{D}-\mathcal{D}_T} \varphi(g) \left( {m E}(s,f_0)(g) - {m E}(s,f_0)_N(g) ight) dg $$ is holomorphic at $s=1/2$. We compute ${m Res}_{s= rac{1}{2}} h_T(s)$ by noting that the second summand of $$  rac{d^n}{d s^n} \left(  rac{T^s}{s} ight) =  rac{(-1)^n n!}{s^{n+1}} + \int_0^{\log T} t^n e^{st} dt $$ is holomorphic at $s=0$, and get $$ {m Res}_{s= rac{1}{2}} h_T(s) = c_i \delta_{\substack{\alpha_i=- rac{1}{2} \ n_i=0}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Rankin-Selberg unfolding of the truncated Eisenstein series; for (4) take residues at $s=1/2$ and let $T\to\infty$ using rapid decay of the non-constant terms.

nodes.name: Regularized integral
nodes.statement: We define the \emph{regularized integral} of a regularizable function $\varphi: [{\rm PGL}_2] \to \ag{C}$ as $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi(g) dg = \frac{1}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} \left( {\rm Res}_{s=\frac{1}{2}} R(s,\varphi) + c_i \delta_{\substack{\alpha_i=-\frac{1}{2} \\ n_i=0}} \right), $$ where $c_i, \alpha_i, n_i$ are associated with $a(t,\varphi)$ as in Definition \ref{RegFuncRDef}. We call the first term the \emph{principal part} of the regularized integral, the second the \emph{degenerate part} of the regularized integral. The regularized integral is linear and extends the integral on $\mathcal{A}^{{\rm reg}}({\rm GL}_2) \cap {\rm L}^1({\rm GL}_2, 1)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\int^{reg}\varphi$ is $\lambda_{\mathbf F}^{(-1)}(0)^{-1}$ times $\mathrm{Res}_{s=1/2}R(s,\varphi)$ plus a degenerate term from the exponent $\alpha_i=-1/2$.
nodes.label: RegIntDef

nodes.name: Finitely regularizable function
nodes.statement:
Let $\omega$ be a unitary character of $\mathbf{F}^{	imes}  ackslash \ag{A}^{	imes}$. Let $\varphi$ be a smooth function on ${m GL}_2(\mathbf{F})  ackslash {m GL}_2(\ag{A})$ with central character $\omega$. We call $\varphi$ \emph{finitely regularizable} if there exist characters $\chi_i: \mathbf{F}^{	imes}  ackslash \ag{A}^{	imes} 	o \ag{C}^{(1)}$, $\alpha_i \in \ag{C}, n_i \in \ag{N}$ and smooth functions $f_i \in {m Ind}_{\gp{B}(\ag{A}) \cap \gp{K}}^{\gp{K}} (\chi_i, \omega \chi_i^{-1})$ for $1 \leq i \leq l$, such that for any $M \gg 1$ $$ \varphi(n(x)a(y)k) = \varphi_{\gp{N}}^*(n(x)a(y)k) + O(
orm[y]_{\ag{A}}^{-M}), 	ext{ as } 
orm[y]_{\ag{A}} 	o \infty, $$ where we have written the \emph{essential constant term} $$ \varphi_{\gp{N}}^*(n(x)a(y)k)=\varphi_{\gp{N}}^*(a(y)k)=\sum_{i=1}^l \chi_i(y) 
orm[y]_{\ag{A}}^{ rac{1}{2}+\alpha_i} \log^{n_i} 
orm[y]_{\ag{A}} f_i(k). $$ In this case, we call $\mathcal{E}{m x}(\varphi)=\{ \chi_i 
orm^{ rac{1}{2}+\alpha_i}: 1 \leq i \leq l \}$ the \emph{exponent set} of $\varphi$, and define $$ \mathcal{E}{m x}^+(\varphi) = \{ \chi_i 
orm^{ rac{1}{2}+\alpha_i} \in \mathcal{E}{m x}(\varphi): \Re \alpha_i \geq 0 \}; \quad \mathcal{E}{m x}^-(\varphi) = \{ \chi_i 
orm^{ rac{1}{2}+\alpha_i} \in \mathcal{E}{m x}(\varphi): \Re \alpha_i < 0 \}. $$ The space of finitely regularizable functions with central character $\omega$ is denoted by $\mathcal{A}^{{m fr}}({m GL}_2,\omega)$.
nodes.genus: smooth function on ${\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$ with central character $\omega$
nodes.statement_short: $\varphi$ is finitely regularizable if it equals a finite sum of characters times $|y|^{1/2+\alpha_i}\log^{n_i}|y|$ (its essential constant term) up to rapid decay; defines the exponent set.
nodes.label: FinRegFuncDef

nodes.name: Finitely regularizable vs regularizable
nodes.statement: In the case $\omega=1$, a finitely regularizable is smooth and regularizable in the sense of Definition \ref{RegFuncDef}. But a smooth regularizable function doesn't need to be finitely regularizable.

nodes.name: Regularizing Eisenstein series
nodes.statement: In the case $\omega^{-1}\xi^2(t)=\norm[t]_{\ag{A}}^{i\mu}$ for some $\mu \in \ag{R}$, we introduce the \emph{regularizing Eisenstein series} for $f \in V_{\xi,\omega\xi^{-1}}^{\infty}$ and $s$ in a neighborhood of $(1-i\mu)/2$ $$ {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(s,f)(g) = {\rm E}(s,f)(g) - \frac{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1-2s-i\mu)}{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s+i\mu)} \int_{\gp{K}} f(\kappa) d\kappa \cdot \chi^{-1}(\det g) \norm[\det g]_{\ag{A}}^{\frac{i\mu}{2}}. $$ It is holomorphic at $s=(1-i\mu)/2$.
nodes.statement_short: $E^{reg}(s,f)$ subtracts from $E(s,f)$ the polar one-dimensional term at $s=(1-i\mu)/2$, making it holomorphic there.
nodes.label: RegEisDef

nodes.name: Hecke operators nearly annihilate the regularizing Eisenstein series
nodes.statement: Let $e_0 \in {\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(1,1)$ be the spherical function taking value $1$ on $\gp{K}$. Let $T(\mathfrak{p})$ denote the order $1$ Hecke operator at a finite place $\mathfrak{p}$ with cardinality of the residue field $q$. For $s \neq 0$, we have $$ T(\mathfrak{p}). {\rm E}(\frac{1}{2}+s, e_0) = \lambda_{\mathfrak{p}}(s) {\rm E}(\frac{1}{2}+s, e_0), \quad \lambda_{\mathfrak{p}}(s) = \frac{q^{1/2+s} + q^{-(1/2+s)}}{q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}}; $$ $$ \text{or} \quad T(\mathfrak{p}). {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}+s, e_0) = \lambda_{\mathfrak{p}}(s) {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}+s, e_0) + (\lambda_{\mathfrak{p}}(s)-1) \cdot \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s). $$ The pole of $\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s)$, defined in (\ref{lambdaFDef}), at $s=0$ is compensated by the zero of $\lambda_{\mathfrak{p}}(s)-1$, hence we get $$ T(\mathfrak{p}). {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}, e_0) = {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}, e_0) + \lambda_{\mathfrak{p}}^{(1)}(0) \cdot \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0). $$ In particular, $(T(\mathfrak{p})-1)^2$ annihilates ${\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(1/2,e_0)$.
nodes.statement_short: $T(\mathfrak p)$ acts on $E^{reg}(1/2,e_0)$ as identity plus a constant, so $(T(\mathfrak p)-1)^2$ kills it.
nodes.label: KillRegEis

nodes.name: Violation of covariance of E^reg
nodes.statement: {(Violation of Covariance)} Unlike the usual Eisenstein series, the map $$ \pi^{\infty}(\xi \norm^{(1-i\mu)/2}, \omega\xi^{-1} \norm^{-(1-i\mu)/2}) \to {\rm C}^{\infty}({\rm GL}_2, \omega), \quad f_{(1-i\mu)/2} \mapsto {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}((1-i\mu)/2, f) $$ is \emph{NOT} ${\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$-covariant. But it's still $\gp{K}$-covariant.

nodes.name: Members of the finitely regularizable space
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{GlobRDEisWhi}, \ref{GlobRDEisCst} and the definition of cusp forms, $\mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ contains: \begin{itemize} \item $\chi(\det g)$ for quasi-characters $\chi$ such that $\chi^2=\omega$; \item smooth cusp forms, i.e., $\mathcal{A}_{{\rm cusp}}^{\infty}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$; \item $\frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n}{\rm E}(s,f)$ for some $n \in \ag{N}$ and smooth $f \in {\rm Ind}_{\gp{B}(\ag{A})}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})}(\xi, \omega\xi^{-1})$ with $\Re s \geq 0$ and $s \neq -i\mu/2, 1/2-i\mu/2$ for $\mu=\mu(\omega^{-1}\xi^2)$ if $\omega\xi^{-2}$ is trivial on $\ag{A}^{(1)}$; \item $\frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} \mid_{s=-i\frac{\mu}{2}} (s+i\frac{\mu}{2}){\rm E}^*(s,f)$ for some $n \in \ag{N}$ and smooth $f$, $\mu$ the same as above; \item $\frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n}{\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1-i\mu}{2},f)$ for some $n \in \ag{N}$ and $f,\mu$ the same as above; \item $\varphi=\Pi_{j=1}^l \varphi_j$ where $\varphi_j \in \mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm GL}_2,\omega_j)$ with $\omega = \Pi_j \omega_j$. \end{itemize} In the last case, we have $ \varphi_{\gp{N}}^* = \Pi_j \varphi_{j,\gp{N}}^* $. Note that we have excluded ${\rm E}(s,f)$ for $\Re s < 0$. But they are actually present since they are related to the case $\Re s > 0$ by functional equation.
nodes.statement_short: Lists functions in $\mathcal A^{fr}$: characters, cusp forms, derivatives of Eisenstein series and of $E^{reg}$, and products.

nodes.name: L^2-residual space
nodes.statement: Let $\omega$ be a unitary character of $\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{\times}$. The ${\rm L}^2$-\emph{residual space} of central character $\omega$, denoted by $\mathcal{E}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$, is the direct sum of the vector spaces $\mathcal{E}^+({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ resp. $\mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ spanned by functions $$ \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}(s,f), \text{if } s \neq \frac{1-i\mu}{2} \quad \text{resp.} \quad \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1-i\mu}{2},f) $$ where $s \in \ag{C}, \Re s > 0$ and for some unitary character $\xi$ of $\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{\times}$, $f \in V_{\xi,\omega\xi^{-1}}^{\infty}$ and $\mu$ as above.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal E(GL_2,\omega)$ is spanned by $s$-derivatives of Eisenstein series with $\Re s>0$ and of regularizing Eisenstein series.

nodes.name: Translation stability of finitely regularizable functions
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ is stable under the right translation by ${\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$. Moreover, for any $\varphi \in \mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ and any $g \in {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$, their sets of exponents are the same: $$ \mathcal{E}{\rm x}(g.\varphi) = \mathcal{E}{\rm x}(\varphi). $$
conclusions: $\mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ is stable under the right translation by ${\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$
$$ \mathcal{E}{\rm x}(g.\varphi) = \mathcal{E}{\rm x}(\varphi). $$
assumptions: for any $\varphi \in \mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ and any $g \in {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$
nodes.label: FregStab

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.20
nodes.statement:
Take $f \in {m Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{m GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(\xi, \omega\xi^{-1})$ and the flat section $f_s \in \pi(\xi

nodes.name: Translation stability of E^+
nodes.statement: The vector space $\mathcal{E}^+({\rm GL}_2, \omega)$ is stable under the right translation by ${\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$.
conclusions: The vector space $\mathcal{E}^+({\rm GL}_2, \omega)$ is stable under the right translation by ${\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.21
nodes.statement: Take a flat section $f_s$ as in the proof of Proposition \ref{FregStab}. Fix $s_0 \in \ag{C}, n \in \ag{N}, g \in {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$ with $\Re s_0 > 0$. Let $e_{\vec{k}}$ be an orthonormal $\gp{K}$-isotypic basis of ${\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(\xi, \omega\xi^{-1})$. There is an orthonormal $\gp{K}$-isotypic basis $\tilde{e}_{\vec{k}}$ of ${\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(\omega\xi^{-1}, \xi)$ and for any $n \in \ag{N}$ there is $A > 0$ such that (c.f. \cite[\S 3]{Wu5}) $$ \mathcal{M}_s e_{\vec{k},s} = \mu_{\vec{k}}(s) \tilde{e}_{\vec{k},-s}, \quad \extnorm{\mu_{\vec{k}}^{(n)}(s)} \ll \lambda_{\vec{k}}^A $$ for some meromorphic function $\mu_{\vec{k}}(s)$, regular in $\Re s > 0, s \neq 1/2$. Here $\lambda_{\vec{k}}$ is the eigenvalue of the Laplacian on $\gp{K}_{\infty}$ for $e_{\vec{k}}$, and the bound is uniform for $s$ lying in any compact subset of the regular region. We also have an expansion $$ g.f_s = \sideset{}{_{\vec{k}}} \sum a_{\vec{k}}(s,g) e_{\vec{k},s}, $$ for some functions $a_{\vec{k}}(s,g)$ holomorphic in $s$ and smooth in $g$, since $$ a_{\vec{k}}(s,g) = \int_{\gp{K}} f_s(\kappa g) \overline{e_{\vec{k}}(\kappa)} d\kappa. $$ Moreover, we have $ a_{\vec{k}}(s,g) \ll_{g,f,N} \lambda_{\vec{k}}^{-N} $ for any $N \in \ag{N}$, uniformly for $s$ lying in any compact neighborhood of $s_0$. It follows that for any $l \in \ag{N}$ $$ a_{\vec{k}}^{(l)}(s,g) := \frac{\partial^l}{\partial s^l} \mid_{s=s_0} a_{\vec{k}}(s,g) \ll_{g,f,N} \lambda_{\vec{k}}^{-N}. $$ We thus get $$ g.f_{s_0}^{(n)} = \sideset{}{_{k=0}^n} \sum \sideset{}{_{\vec{k}}} \sum \binom{n}{k} a_{\vec{k}}^{(n-k)}(s_0,g) e_{\vec{k},s_0}^{(k)}. $$ The inner sum coincides with the value at $s=s_0$ of a flat section $f_{k,s}^{(k)}$ defined by $$ f_k = \binom{n}{k} \sideset{}{_{\vec{k}}} \sum a_{\vec{k}}^{(n-k)}(s_0,g) e_{\vec{k}}, $$ which is smooth. We can also verify that \begin{align*} \sideset{}{_{k=0}^n} \sum \frac{\partial^k}{\partial s^k} \mid_{s=s_0} \mathcal{M}_s f_{k,s} &= \sideset{}{_{k=0}^n} \sum \sideset{}{_{\vec{k}}} \sum \binom{n}{k} a_{\vec{k}}^{(n-k)}(s_0,g) \frac{\partial^k}{\partial s^k} \mid_{s=s_0} (\mu_{\vec{k}}(s) \tilde{e}_{\vec{k},-s}) \\ &= \sideset{}{_{\vec{k}}} \sum \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} \mid_{s=s_0} (a_{\vec{k}}(s,g) \mu_{\vec{k}}(s) \tilde{e}_{\vec{k},-s}) = \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} \mid_{s=s_0} \mathcal{M}_s f_s, \end{align*} hence we deduce that $$ g.{\rm E}_{\gp{N}}^{(n)}(s_0,f) = \sideset{}{_{k=0}^n} \sum {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}^{(k)}(s_0,f_k). $$ We conclude by $$ g.{\rm E}^{(n)}(s_0,f) = \sideset{}{_{k=0}^n} \sum {\rm E}^{(k)}(s_0,f_k) $$ since both sides are orthogonal to the cusp forms and have the same constant term.
nodes.statement_short: Expand $g.f_s$ in a $K$-isotypic basis with rapidly decaying coefficients, match constant terms via the intertwining operator, and conclude by orthogonality to cusp forms.

nodes.name: Coincidence of the constructed f_k
nodes.statement: $f_k$ constructed in both proofs of Proposition \ref{FregStab} and \ref{Reis+Stab} coincide with each other.

Choose a finite place $\mathfrak{p}_0$ with uniformizer $\varpi_0$. Let $e_0 \in {m Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{m GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(1,1)$ be the spherical function taking value $1$ on $\gp{K}$. eq 0, $$ hence $0

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of the L^2-residue
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi \in \mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$. \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] We can always find (not unique) $\mathcal{E}(\varphi) \in \mathcal{E}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ such that $\varphi - \mathcal{E}(\varphi) \in {\rm L}^1({\rm GL}_2, \omega)$. \item[(2)] If for any $\chi \in \mathcal{E}{\rm x}(\varphi)$, we have $\Re \chi \neq 1/2$, then there is a unique function $\mathcal{E}(\varphi) \in \mathcal{E}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ such that $\varphi - \mathcal{E}(\varphi) \in {\rm L}^2({\rm GL}_2, \omega)$. nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.24
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{IntExpBd} and Proposition \ref{GlobRDEisWhi}, it is not difficult to see that $\mathcal{E}({\rm GL}_2,\omega) \cap {\rm L}^2({\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}), \omega) = \{0\}$, which implies the uniqueness of $\mathcal{E}(\varphi)$ in (2). For the existence, we find $\chi_i, \alpha_i, n_i, f_i$ as in Definition \ref{FinRegFuncDef}. Then we take, writing $\mu_i = \mu(\omega^{-1}\chi_i^2)$, \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(\varphi) = \sum_{\substack{\Re \alpha_j > 0 \\ \alpha_j \neq \frac{1}{2}+i\mu_j}} \frac{\partial^{n_j}}{\partial s^{n_j}}{\rm E}(\alpha_j,\omega,\omega^{-1}\chi_j;f_j) + \sum_{\substack{\Re \alpha_j > 0 \\ \alpha_j = \frac{1}{2}+i\mu_j}} \frac{\partial^{n_j}}{\partial s^{n_j}}{\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\alpha_j,\omega,\omega^{-1}\chi_j;f_j). \end{equation} Thus for any $\chi \in \mathcal{E}{\rm x}(\varphi-\mathcal{E}(\varphi))$, we have $\Re \chi \leq 1/2$ resp. $\Re \chi < 1/2$ under the condition in (2). Hence $\varphi-\mathcal{E}(\varphi) \in {\rm L}^1({\rm GL}_2, \omega)$ resp. ${\rm L}^2({\rm GL}_2, \omega)$. For the ``moreover'' part, it suffices to see that the differential operator $X$ does not increase the real part of elements in $\mathcal{E}{\rm x}(\varphi)$, which is essentially due to the following calculation: $$ y \frac{d}{dy} (y^{\sigma} \log^k y) = y^{\sigma} \log^k y + k y^{\sigma} \log^{k-1}y, \forall y>0, \sigma \in \ag{C}, k \in \ag{N}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Uniqueness: $\mathcal E\cap L^2=0$; existence: subtract explicit (regularizing) Eisenstein series matching each exponent with $\Re\alpha_j>0$.

nodes.name: Explicit L^2-residue
nodes.statement: \mathcal{E}(\varphi) = \sum_{\substack{\Re \alpha_j > 0 \\ \alpha_j \neq \frac{1}{2}+i\mu_j}} \frac{\partial^{n_j}}{\partial s^{n_j}}{\rm E}(\alpha_j,\omega,\omega^{-1}\chi_j;f_j) + \sum_{\substack{\Re \alpha_j > 0 \\ \alpha_j = \frac{1}{2}+i\mu_j}} \frac{\partial^{n_j}}{\partial s^{n_j}}{\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\alpha_j,\omega,\omega^{-1}\chi_j;f_j).
nodes.statement_short: Explicit $\mathcal E(\varphi)$ as a sum of derivatives of Eisenstein and regularizing Eisenstein series.
nodes.label: ReisDef

nodes.name: L^2-residue
nodes.statement: In the case (2), we call $\mathcal{E}(\varphi)$ the ${\rm L}^2$-residue of $\varphi$. For definiteness, we shall write $\mathcal{E}(\varphi)$ to be the one given by (\ref{ReisDef}).

nodes.name: Vanishing on residual space and invariance of the regularized integral
nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] For any $\mathcal{E} \in \mathcal{E}({\rm GL}_2,1)$, we have $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \mathcal{E}(g) dg = 0. $$ If moreover $\mathcal{E} \in \mathcal{E}^+({\rm GL}_2,1)$, then for any $g_0 \in {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$, we have $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} g_0.\mathcal{E}(g) dg = 0. $$ \item[(2)] Let $\varphi \in \mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm GL}_2,1)$. For any $\mathcal{E} \in \mathcal{E}({\rm GL}_2,1)$ such that $\varphi - \mathcal{E} \in {\rm L}^1([{\rm PGL}_2])$ we have $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi(g) dg = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} (\varphi-\mathcal{E})(g) dg. $$ In particular, $\int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}}$ is always $\gp{K}$-invariant. It is ${\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$-invariant on the subspace of $\varphi \in \mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm GL}_2,1)$ such that $\mathcal{E}{\rm x}(\varphi)$ does not contain $\norm_{\ag{A}}$. \end{itemize}

conclusions: $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \mathcal{E}(g) dg = 0. $$
$$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} g_0.\mathcal{E}(g) dg = 0. $$

assumptions: For any $\mathcal{E} \in \mathcal{E}({\rm GL}_2,1)$ such that $\varphi - \mathcal{E} \in {\rm L}^1([{\rm PGL}_2])$
conclusions: $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi(g) dg = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} (\varphi-\mathcal{E})(g) dg. $$
In particular, $\int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}}$ is always $\gp{K}$-invariant.

assumptions: For any $\mathcal{E} \in \mathcal{E}({\rm GL}_2,1)$ such that $\varphi - \mathcal{E} \in {\rm L}^1([{\rm PGL}_2])$
conclusions: $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \mathcal{E}(g) dg = 0. $$
$$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} g_0.\mathcal{E}(g) dg = 0. $$
$$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi(g) dg = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} (\varphi-\mathcal{E})(g) dg. $$
In particular, $\int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}}$ is always $\gp{K}$-invariant.
nodes.statement_short: The regularized integral kills the residual space, equals the ordinary integral of $\varphi-\mathcal E$, is $K$-invariant, and $GL_2(\mathbb A)$-invariant away from the singular exponent.
nodes.label: RegGInv

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.26
nodes.statement: For (1), the second assertion follows from the first by Proposition \ref{Reis+Stab}. We calculate $a(t,\mathcal{E})$ for $\mathcal{E}(g) = \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}(s,f)(gg_0)$ with $s \neq 1/2-i\mu(\chi)$ resp. $\frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}-i\mu(\chi),f)(g)$ for some $f \in V_{\chi,\chi^{-1}}^{\infty}$ with $\Re s > 0$, a unitary character $\chi$ of $\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{\times}$ if $\chi \mid_{\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{(1)}} = 1$. Due to the integral $\int_{\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{(1)}} d^{\times}y$, it is easy to see that $a(t,\varphi)$ is non-vanishing only if $\chi$ is trivial on $\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{(1)}$, in which case $\mu(\omega\chi^2)=2\mu(\chi)$. We also notice that we can interchange the order of $\mathcal{M}$ and $\int_{\gp{K}} dk$ since they commute with each other. \begin{itemize} \item $\mathcal{E}(g) = \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}(s,f)(g)$ with $s \neq 1/2-i\mu(\chi)$: We get $$ a(t,\mathcal{E}) = \zeta_{\mathbf{F}}^*(1) \int_{\gp{K}} f(k)dk \cdot \left\{ t^{\frac{1}{2}+s+i\mu(\chi)} \log^n t + \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} \left( t^{\frac{1}{2}-s-i\mu(\chi)} \frac{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1-2s-2i\mu(\chi))}{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s+2i\mu(\chi))} \right) \right\}, $$ and conclude by the fact that $a(t,\mathcal{E})$ has no constant term as a function of $t$. \item $\mathcal{E}(g)=\frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}-i\mu(\chi),f)(g)$: We get \begin{align*} a(t,\mathcal{E}) &= \zeta_{\mathbf{F}}^*(1) \int_{\gp{K}} f(k)dk \cdot \\ &\quad \left\{ t \log^n t + \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} \mid_{s=\frac{1}{2}-i\mu(\chi)} \left( (t^{\frac{1}{2}-s-i\mu(\chi)}-1) \frac{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1-2s-2i\mu(\chi))}{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s+2i\mu(\chi))} \right) \right\} \\ &= \zeta_{\mathbf{F}}^*(1) \int_{\gp{K}} f(k)dk \cdot \\ &\quad \left\{ t \log^n t + \sum_{l=0}^n \binom{n}{l} \frac{(-1)^l}{l+1} \cdot \log^{l+1}t \cdot \frac{d^{n-l}}{d s^{n-l}} \mid_{s=0} \left( \frac{s\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(2s)}{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(2-2s)} \right) \right\}, \end{align*} and conclude the same way as in the previous case. \end{itemize} For (2), the first part is trivial. For the second part, we note that $\varphi-\mathcal{E}(\varphi) \in {\rm L}^1$ implies $g_0.\varphi-g_0.\mathcal{E}(\varphi) \in {\rm L}^1$ for any $g_0 \in {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$, and $g_0.\mathcal{E}(\varphi)$ has regularized integral $0$ by (1) if either $\mathcal{E} \in \mathcal{E}^+({\rm GL}_2,1)$ or $g_0 \in \gp{K}$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute the regularizing kernel $a(t,\mathcal E)$ for each generator of the residual space and observe it has no constant term; (2) follows from (1).

nodes.name: Comparison with Michel-Venkatesh proof
nodes.statement: The above proof of (2) is to be compared with \cite[\S 4.3.6]{MV10}, where another simpler but indirect proof was given for the ``regular case''.

nodes.name: Regularized integral of product of two Eisenstein series, regular case
nodes.statement: Let $\xi_j,\xi_j'$ be (unitary) Hecke characters with $\xi_1\xi_1' \xi_2 \xi_2' = 1$ and write $\pi_j = \pi(\xi_j,\xi_j')$, $j=1,2$. For $f_j \in \pi_j$, we shall write ${\rm E}^{\sharp}$ for ${\rm E}$ or ${\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}$, whichever is regular at $s=1/2$. If $\pi_1 \not \simeq \widetilde{\pi_2}$, then for any $n_1, n_2 \in \ag{N}$, we have $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{(n_1)}(0,f_1) {\rm E}^{(n_2)}(0,f_2) = 0, \quad \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{\sharp,(n_1)}(1/2,f_1) {\rm E}^{\sharp,(n_2)}(1/2,f_2) = 0. $$
assumptions: Let $\xi_j,\xi_j'$ be (unitary) Hecke characters with $\xi_1\xi_1' \xi_2 \xi_2' = 1$ and write $\pi_j = \pi(\xi_j,\xi_j')$, $j=1,2$.
nodes.statement_short: For non-dual $\pi_1,\pi_2$, regularized integrals of products of derivatives of Eisenstein series at $0$ or $1/2$ vanish.
nodes.label: SimpleProd

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: $R(s, {\rm E}^{(n_1)}(0,f_1) {\rm E}^{(n_2)}(0,f_2))$ resp. $R(s, {\rm E}^{\sharp,(n_1)}(1/2,f_1) {\rm E}^{\sharp,(n_2)}(1/2,f_2))$ represents the value at $s_1=s_2=0$ of $\partial_1^{n_1} \partial_2^{n_2}$ of $$ \Lambda(1/2+s+s_1+s_2, \xi_1\xi_2) \Lambda(1/2+s+s_1-s_2, \xi_1\xi_2') \Lambda(1/2+s-s_1+s_2, \xi_1'\xi_2) \Lambda(1/2+s-s_1-s_2, \xi_1'\xi_2') \quad \text{resp.} $$ $$ \Lambda(3/2+s+s_1+s_2, \xi_1\xi_2) \Lambda(1/2+s+s_1-s_2, \xi_1\xi_2') \Lambda(1/2+s-s_1+s_2, \xi_1'\xi_2) \Lambda(-1/2+s-s_1-s_2, \xi_1'\xi_2'), $$ which is regular at $s=1/2$ by assumption. The degenerate part is also easily seen to be $0$ by assumption. We conclude by Definition \ref{RegIntDef}.
nodes.statement_short: $R(s,\cdot)$ is a product of four completed $L$-functions regular at $s=1/2$; the degenerate part vanishes; apply Definition 2.12.

nodes.name: Deformation principle
nodes.statement_short: If $\varphi-\mathcal E$ is integrable and both deform continuously, $\int^{reg}\varphi$ is the limit of differences of regularized integrals of the deformations.

nodes.name: Deformation principle formula
nodes.statement: \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi - \mathcal{E} = \lim_{s \to 0} \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi_s - \mathcal{E}_s = \lim_{s \to 0} \left( \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi_s - \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \mathcal{E}_s \right).
nodes.label: DeformTec

nodes.name: Normalized intertwining operator M_s
nodes.statement: If $f \in {\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(\xi_1,\xi_2)$, we define for any $s \in \ag{C}$ an operator $\mathcal{M}_s: {\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(\xi_1,\xi_2) \to {\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(\xi_2,\xi_1)$ (abuse of notations) by requiring $$ \mathcal{M}_s f_s(a(y)\kappa) = \xi_2(y)\norm[y]_{\ag{A}}^{\frac{1}{2}-s} \mathcal{M}_sf(\kappa), \quad \text{i.e.,} \quad \mathcal{M}_s f_s = (\mathcal{M}_s f)_{-s}; $$ $$ \text{resp.} \quad \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_s = \mathcal{M}_s \circ (I-{\rm P}_{\gp{K}}e_{\xi}), \quad \text{if } \xi_1=\xi_2=\xi $$ with the Taylor expansion at $s=0$ resp. $s=1/2$ when $\xi_1=\xi_2 = \xi$ (since $\mathcal{M}_s$ is ``diagonalizable'') $$ \mathcal{M}_sf = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{s^n}{n!} \mathcal{M}_0^{(n)}f, \quad \text{resp.} \quad \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2+s} f = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{s^n}{n!} \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2}^{(n)}f. $$ Here ${\rm P}_{\gp{K}}$, with $d\kappa$ the probability Haar measure on $\gp{K}$, is defined to be the map $$ \pi(\xi,\xi) \to \ag{C}, f \mapsto \int_{\gp{K}} f(\kappa) \xi^{-1}(\kappa) d\kappa, $$ and $e_{\xi} = \xi \circ \det \in {\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(\xi,\xi)$.
nodes.statement_short: Defines the intertwining operator $\mathcal M_s$ on $K$-restrictions, its modification $\widetilde{\mathcal M}_s$, their Taylor coefficients, and the projection $P_K$.

nodes.name: Vanishing of product with derivative, unitary case
nodes.statement: Let $f_1,f_2 \in {\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(1,1)$. For $0 \neq s \in \ag{C}$ small, we have $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}(s,f_1) {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_2) = 0. $$
nodes.label: SimpleProdU

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement: This is a variant of Lemma \ref{SimpleProd}.
nodes.statement_short: Variant of the argument for Lemma 3.1.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.4 (2) by deformation
nodes.statement:
We continue to use the notations in the previous lemma. We can write
	$$ {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}(s,f_1) {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}^{(1)}(0,f_2) = 2(f_1f_2)_{1/2+s}^{(1)} + 2(\mathcal{M}_s f_1f_2)_{1/2-s}^{(1)} + (f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2)_{1/2+s} + (\mathcal{M}_s f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2)_{1/2-s}. $$
	We tentatively define
\begin{align*}
	\mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) &:= s^{-1} \left\{ 2 {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(1)}(1/2+s, f_1f_2) + 2 {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(1)}(1/2-s, \mathcal{M}_s f_1f_2) \right. \\
	 &\left. + {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(1/2+s, f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) + {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(1/2-s, \mathcal{M}_s f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) \right\}
\end{align*}
	Applying Lemma \ref{SimpleProdU}, \ref{SimpleProdSing} with $n=0, 1$ together with (\ref{DeformTec}), we get
\begin{align*}
	\int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_1) {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_2) &= \lim_{s \to 0} \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} s^{-1} {\rm E}(s,f_1) {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_2) - \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) \\
	&= \frac{1}{s} \cdot \left\{ 2 \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(1)}(s)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1f_2) + 2  \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(1)}(-s)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_s f_1f_2) \right. \\
	&\left. + \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) + \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(-s)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_s f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) \right\}.
\end{align*}
	Taking Laurent expansions, we verify that the function in $s$ in the range of the above limit is regular at $s=0$, unlike its appearance. The properties
	$$ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(k)}f_2) = {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_2 \mathcal{M}_0^{(k)}f_1), \forall k \in \ag{N}; \quad \mathcal{M}_0^{(2)} = \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)} \circ \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)} $$
	$$ \text{coming from} \quad \mathcal{M}_s \circ \mathcal{M}_{-s} = 1 $$
must be used. Taking limit as $s \to 0$, we obtain (2) of the following:
nodes.statement_short: Deform $E^{(1)}(0,f_1)$ to $s^{-1}E(s,f_1)$, subtract a tentative regularizing combination $\mathcal E^{reg}(s)$, apply Lemmas 3.3, 3.6 and (3.1), and take the limit $s\to0$ via Laurent expansions.

nodes.name: Regularized integral of product of two unitary Eisenstein series
nodes.statement: If $\pi(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ is spherical, we also write The regularized integral of the product of two unitary Eisenstein series is computed as: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] If $\pi_1 = \pi(\xi_1,\xi_2), \pi_2 = \pi(\xi_1^{-1}, \xi_2^{-1})$ resp. $\pi_2 = \pi(\xi_2^{-1}, \xi_1^{-1})$ and $\xi_1 \neq \xi_2$, then $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}(0,f_1) {\rm E}(0,f_2) = \frac{2\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(0)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1f_2) - {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0 f_2), \quad \text{resp.} $$ $$ \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(0)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} ({\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1 \mathcal{M}_0 f_2) + {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_2 \mathcal{M}_0 f_1)) - {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot f_2). $$ \item[(2)] If $\pi_1 = \pi(\xi,\xi), \pi_2 = \pi(\xi^{-1},\xi^{-1})$, then \begin{align*} &\quad \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_1) {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_2) = \frac{4\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(2)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{-1}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1f_2) + \frac{4\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(2)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{-1}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)} f_2) \\ &\quad + \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(0)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{-1}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) - \frac{1}{3} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(3)}f_1 \cdot f_2) - {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(2)}f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2). \end{align*} \end{itemize}

conclusions: $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}(0,f_1) {\rm E}(0,f_2) = \frac{2\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(0)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1f_2) - {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0 f_2), \quad \text{resp.} $$

$$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}(0,f_1) {\rm E}(0,f_2) = \frac{2\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(0)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1f_2) - {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0 f_2), \quad \text{resp.} $$
nodes.statement_short: Explicit formulas for $\int^{reg}E(0,f_1)E(0,f_2)$ and, in the doubly singular unitary case, $\int^{reg}E^{(1)}(0,f_1)E^{(1)}(0,f_2)$ via $P_K$ and derivatives of $\mathcal M_0$.
nodes.label: RIPEisUnitary

nodes.name: Formulas for higher derivatives omitted
nodes.statement: It is possible to get formulas for all derivatives, exploiting more the relation $\mathcal{M}_s \circ \mathcal{M}_{-s} = 1$. Since we don't have applications of these formulas, we do not include them here.

nodes.name: Regularized integrals involving E^reg near 1/2
nodes.statement: Let $f, f_1, f_2 \in {\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(1,1)$. For $0 \neq s \in \ag{C}$ small, we have for any $n, n_1, n_2 \in \ag{N}$ $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}, (n)}(\frac{1}{2}+s, f) = -\frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(n)}(s)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f); $$ $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}, (n_1)}(\frac{1}{2}+s, f_1) {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}, (n_2)}(\frac{1}{2}, f_2) = 0. $$
conclusions: $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}, (n)}(\frac{1}{2}+s, f) = -\frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(n)}(s)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f); $$
nodes.label: SimpleProdSing

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.6
nodes.statement: The first formula follows immediately from Proposition \ref{RegGInv} and definition. The second one is a variant of Lemma \ref{SimpleProd}.
nodes.statement_short: First formula from Proposition 2.26 and the definition; second as a variant of Lemma 3.1.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.7 (3) by deformation
nodes.statement:
We continue to use the notations in the previous section and lemma. Denote $e=e_1$. We can write
	$$ {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}^{{\rm reg}}(s,f) = f_s + (\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_s f)_{-s} + \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s-\frac{1}{2}) {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f) \left( e_{-s} - e_{-1/2} \right); $$
\begin{align*}
	{\rm E}_{\gp{N}}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(\frac{1}{2},f) &= f_{1/2}^{(n)} + \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k} (-1)^k (\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2}^{(n-k)} f)_{-1/2}^{(k)} \\
	&+ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f) \cdot \left\{ \frac{(-1)^{n+1} \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{-1)}(0)}{n+1} e_{-1/2}^{(n+1)} + \sum_{k=1}^n \binom{n}{k} (-1)^k \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(n-k)}(0) e_{-1/2}^k \right\},
\end{align*}
from which one easily deduce ${\rm E}_{\gp{N}}^{{\rm reg}}(1/2+s,f_1) {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}^{{\rm reg},(n_2)}(1/2,f_2)$. We tentatively define
\begin{align*}
	\mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) &:= {\rm E}^{(n_2)}(\frac{3}{2}+s, f_1f_2) + \sum_{k=0}^{n_2} \binom{n_2}{k} (-1)^k {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}, (k)}(\frac{1}{2}+s, f_1 \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2}^{(n_2-k)} f_2) \\
	&\quad + {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_2) \cdot \left\{ \frac{(-1)^{n_2+1} \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)}{n_2+1} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n_2+1)}(\frac{1}{2}+s, f_1) \right. \\
	&\quad \left. + \sum_{k=1}^{n_2} \binom{n_2}{k} (-1)^k \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(n_2-k)}(0) {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(k)}(\frac{1}{2}+s, f_1) \right\} \\
	&\quad + {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n_2)}(\frac{1}{2}-s, f_2 \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2+s}f_1) \\
	&\quad + \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s) {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1) \cdot \left\{ {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n_2)}(\frac{1}{2}-s, f_2) - {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n_2)}(\frac{1}{2}, f_2) \right\}.
\end{align*}
	Applying Lemma \ref{SimpleProdSing} with $n_1=0$ together with (\ref{DeformTec}), we get
\begin{align*}
	&\quad \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2},f_1) {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n_2)}(\frac{1}{2},f_2) = \lim_{s \to 0} \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}+s,f_1) {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n_2)}(\frac{1}{2},f_2) - \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) \\

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.2
nodes.statement: The case (1) being simpler, we only give details for (2). By twisting, we may assume $\xi=1$. Let $s$ be small with $\Re s < 0$. The ${\rm L}^2$-residue of $\varphi \cdot {\rm E}(1/2+s,f)$ is given by $$ \mathcal{E}(s) := \sideset{}{_j} \sum {\rm E}^{(n_j)}(s+1+\alpha_j, f_j f), $$ where the summation is over $j$ such that $\Re \alpha_j > -1$. Define $$ \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) := \sideset{}{_j'} \sum {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n_j)}(s+1+\alpha_j, f_j f) + \sideset{}{_j^*} \sum {\rm E}^{(n_j)}(s+1+\alpha_j, f_j f) $$ where $\sideset{}{_j'} \sum$ is the summation as in the statement and $\sideset{}{_j^*} \sum$ is the rest. By the previous proposition, we have \begin{align*} R(\frac{1}{2}+s,\varphi;f) &= \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi \cdot {\rm E}(\frac{1}{2}+s,f) = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}+s,f) + \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s) {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f) \cdot \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi \\ &= \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \left( \varphi \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}+s,f) - \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) \right) - \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \left( \mathcal{E}(s) - \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) \right) \\ &\quad + \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s) {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f) \cdot \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi. \end{align*} Since $\mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(s)$ is the ${\rm L}^2$-residue of $\varphi \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(\frac{1}{2}+s,f)$, we can compare the holomorphic part of both sides and conclude by $$ \mathcal{E}(s) - \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) = \sideset{}{_j'} \sum \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(n_j)}(s) {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_jf). $$
nodes.statement_short: Twist to $\xi=1$; subtract the $L^2$-residue of $\varphi E(1/2+s,f)$, apply Proposition 4.1 and compare holomorphic parts.

nodes.name: A singular triple product formula
nodes.statement: Let $f_j \in \pi(1,1), j=1,2,3$. Then for any $n \in \ag{N}$ $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^*(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^*(0,f_2) \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(\frac{1}{2},f_3) $$ is the sum of $$ \left( \frac{\partial^n R}{\partial s^n} \right)^{{\rm hol}}(\frac{1}{2}, {\rm E}^*(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^*(0,f_2); f_3) $$ and a weighted sum with coefficients depending only on $\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s)$ of $$ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(l)}f_1 \cdot f_2) {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_3), \quad 0 \leq l \leq 3; $$ $$ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1\cdot f_2 \cdot \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2}^{(l)} f_3), \quad 0 \leq l \leq \max(2,n) \quad \& \quad l = n+3; $$ $$ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}((f_1 \mathcal{M}_0 f_2 + f_2 \mathcal{M}_0 f_1) \cdot \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2}^{(l)} f_3), \quad 0 \leq l \leq \max(1,n) \quad \& \quad l = n+2; $$ $$ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0 f_1\cdot \mathcal{M}_0 f_2 \cdot \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2}^{(l)} f_3), \quad 0 \leq l \leq n \quad \& \quad l = n+1. $$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.3
nodes.statement: We shall only point out how the computation is effectuated, since the formulas are quite long. \begin{align*} \mathcal{E}(f_1,f_2) &:= (\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^*)^2 \cdot \left\{ {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(2)}(\frac{1}{2},f_1f_2) + \frac{1}{2} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(1)}(\frac{1}{2}, f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2 + \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot f_2) \right. \\ &\quad\left. + \frac{1}{4} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}, \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) \right\} \end{align*} is the ${\rm L}^2$-residue of ${\rm E}^*(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^*(0,f_2)$. Let $\varphi := {\rm E}^*(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^*(0,f_2) - \mathcal{E}(f_1,f_2)$, then we need to compute $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(\frac{1}{2},f_3) + \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \mathcal{E}(f_1,f_2) \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(\frac{1}{2},f_3). $$ The first term is computed by Proposition \ref{TripleToDouble} (2), involving $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^*(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^*(0,f_2) = \frac{(\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^*)^2}{4} \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_2), $$ which is treated in Theorem \ref{RIPEisUnitary} (2). The second term is treated in Theorem \ref{RIPEisSing} (3).
nodes.statement_short: Split $E^*E^*$ into its $L^2$-residue and an integrable rest; treat the rest by Proposition 4.2(2) and the residue part by Theorems 3.4(2) and 3.7(3).

nodes.name: Section of the adelic norm and triviality of characters
nodes.statement: Namely we fix a section $s_{\mathbf{F}}: \ag{R}_+ \to \mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{\times}$ and assume the Hecke characters $\omega, \xi$ to be trivial on the image of $s_{\mathbf{F}}$.

nodes.name: Abbreviated Eisenstein series notation
nodes.statement: We will sometimes omit $\xi,\omega\xi^{-1}$ and write ${\rm E}(s,f)$ when it is clear from the context.

nodes.name: Constant term E_N of the Eisenstein series
nodes.statement:
Precisely, we shall decompose it as
	$$ {\rm E}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f) = {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f) + \left( {\rm E}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f) - {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f) \right) \text{ with} $$
	$$ {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)(g) := \int_{\mathbf{F} \backslash \ag{A}} {\rm E}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)(n(x)g) dx, n(x) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & x \\ & 1 \end{pmatrix} $$
and study the growth in $g$ of ${\rm E}_{\gp{N}}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)$ and ${\rm E}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f) - {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)$ separately, as well as all their derivatives with respect to $s$.

nodes.name: Whittaker function W of the Eisenstein series
nodes.statement:
We focus on
	$$ {\rm E}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)(g) - {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)(g) = \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbf{F}^{\times}} W(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)(a(\alpha)g) \text{ with } a(\alpha)=\begin{pmatrix} \alpha & \\ & 1 \end{pmatrix} $$
	$$ \text{and} \quad W(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)(g) = \int_{\mathbf{F} \backslash \ag{A}} \psi(-x) {\rm E}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)(n(x)g) dx, $$
where $\psi$ is the standard additive character of $\mathbf{F} \backslash \ag{A}$.

nodes.name: Section f_Phi attached to a Schwartz function
nodes.statement:
If $\Phi \in \mathcal{S}(\ag{A}^2)$ is a Schwartz function, we can define the following (non flat) section in $V_{s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1}}^{\infty}$
	$$ f_{\Phi}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};g) = \xi(\det g)\norm[\det g]_{\ag{A}}^{\frac{1}{2}+s} \int_{\ag{A}^{\times}} \Phi((0,t)g) \omega^{-1}\xi^2(t) \norm[t]_{\ag{A}}^{1+2s} d^{\times}t $$
first defined for $\Re s > 0$ then meromorphically continued to $s \in \ag{C}$.
nodes.statement_short: Godement-type section $f_\Phi$: twisted Tate integral of $\Phi((0,t)g)$, continued meromorphically.

nodes.name: Schwartz function Phi associated with f
nodes.statement:
Given $f \in V_{0,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1}}^{\infty}$, we want to give an explicit $\Phi$ associated with $f$. For simplicity of notations, we may assume $f$ to be a pure tensor. We then construct $\Phi = \otimes_v' \Phi_v$ place by place:

\noindent (1) At $\mathbf{F}_v = \ag{C}$ resp. $\mathbf{F}_v = \ag{R}$ and for $f_v$ spherical resp. not spherical, we choose $\Phi_v$ using the construction in \cite[Lemma 3.5 (1)]{Wu5} resp. \cite[Lemma 3.8 (1)]{Wu5} for spherical resp. smooth functions.

\noindent (2) At $v < \infty$ and for $f_v$ not spherical, we choose $\Phi_v$ by
	$$ \Phi_v((0,1) \kappa) = \mathbf{C}(\psi_v)\xi_v(\det \kappa)^{-1}f_v(\kappa), \kappa \in \gp{K}_v \text{ i.e.} $$
	$$ \Phi_v(ux,u) = \mathbf{C}(\psi_v)\omega_v \xi_v^2(u) f_v \begin{pmatrix} 1 & \\ x & 1 \end{pmatrix}, \forall u \in \mathfrak{o}_v^{\times}, x \in \mathfrak{o}_v; $$
	$$ \Phi_v(u,uy) = \mathbf{C}(\psi_v)\omega_v \xi_v^2(u) f_v \begin{pmatrix} & -1 \\ 1 & y \end{pmatrix}, \forall u \in \mathfrak{o}_v^{\times}, y \in \varpi_v \mathfrak{o}_v; $$
	and $\Phi_v(x,y)=0$ for $\max(\norm[x]_v,\norm[y]_v) \neq 1$.
	
\noindent (3) At $v < \infty$ and for $f_v$ spherical, we choose $\Phi_v$ by
	$$ \Phi_v = \mathbf{C}(\psi_v) \cdot f_v(1) \cdot 1_{\mathfrak{o}_v^2}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Place-by-place choice of $\Phi_v$ (archimedean via [Wu5], ramified via $f_v$ on $K_v$, unramified as $f_v(1)1_{\mathfrak o_v^2}$).

nodes.name: Set S(f) of non-spherical places
nodes.statement: Let $S=S(f)$ be the set of places $v$ such that $f_v$ is not spherical.

nodes.statement: By integration by parts we get $$ \Mellin{f}(s) = \frac{(-1)^k}{s(s+1) \cdots (s+k-1)} \int_0^{\infty} f^{(k)}(y) y^{s+k} \frac{dy}{y}, $$ from which it follows readily that $H_{\infty}^{k,\sigma}(\Mellin{f}) \leq B_1^{k,\sigma}(f)$. nodes.name: Angular Fourier components f_xi
nodes.statement: We write the multiplicative group $\mathbf{F}^1 = \{ x \in \mathbf{F}: \norm[x]_{\mathbf{F}} = 1 \}$. For any function $f$ on $\mathbf{F}^{\times}$ and any character $\xi \in \widehat{\mathbf{F}^1}$ we define a function on $\ag{R}_+$ $$ f_{\xi}(t) = f(t;\xi) = \int_{\mathbf{F}^1} f(tu) \xi(u) du, t > 0 $$ where $du$ is the probability Haar measure on $\mathbf{F}^1$. Concretely: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] If $\mathbf{F}=\ag{R}$ then $\mathbf{F}^1=\{ \pm 1\}, \widehat{\mathbf{F}^1}=\{ \xi_+, \xi_- \}$ with $\xi_+ \equiv 1$ and $\xi_-(-1)=-1$. We then define $$ f(t;+) = f_+(t) = \frac{1}{2} \left( f(t) + f(-t) \right), f(t;-) = f_-(t) = \frac{1}{2} \left( f(t) - f(-t) \right). $$ \item[(2)] If $\mathbf{F}=\ag{C}$ then $\mathbf{F}^1=\{ e^{i \theta}: \theta \in \ag{R}/2\pi \ag{Z} \}, \widehat{\mathbf{F}^1}=\{ \xi_n: n \in \ag{Z} \}$ with $\xi_n(e^{i\theta}) = e^{i n \theta}$. We then define $$ f(t;n) = f_n(t) = \int_{\ag{R} / 2\pi \ag{Z}} f(te^{i\theta}) e^{in\theta} \frac{d\theta}{2\pi}. $$ \end{itemize}

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.15
nodes.statement: In the case $\mathbf{F}=\ag{R}$, we have $$ t^k\frac{d^k}{dt^k} f(t;+) = \frac{1}{2} \left( t^kf^{(k)}(t) + (-1)^k t^k f^{(k)}(-t) \right), $$ $$ t^k\frac{d^k}{dt^k} f(t;-) = \frac{1}{2} \left( t^kf^{(k)}(t) + (-1)^{k+1} t^k f^{(k)}(-t) \right), $$ from which it is easy to see $$ B_{\infty}^{k,\sigma}(f_{\pm}) \leq \mathcal{S}_{\infty}^{\lfloor k+\sigma \rfloor, k}(f) + \mathcal{S}_{\infty}^{\lceil k+\sigma \rceil, k}(f), \forall k \in \ag{N}, \sigma > 0. $$ In the case $\mathbf{F}=\ag{C}$, with the Cartesian \& Polar coordinates $$ (x,y) = (t \cos \theta, t \sin \theta), (z,\bar{z})=(x+iy,x-iy) $$ we have $$ \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} = i \left( z \frac{\partial}{\partial z} - \bar{z} \frac{\partial}{\partial \bar{z}} \right); t\frac{\partial}{\partial t} = z \frac{\partial}{\partial z} + \bar{z} \frac{\partial}{\partial \bar{z}}. $$ By induction on $k \in \ag{N}$, it is easy to see $$ t^k \frac{\partial^k}{\partial t^k} = P_k(z \frac{\partial}{\partial z} + \bar{z} \frac{\partial}{\partial \bar{z}}) $$ for some polynomial $P_k \in \ag{Z}[X]$ and any $k \in \ag{N}$. It follows that \begin{align*} t^k f_n^{(k)}(t) &= \int_{\ag{R} / 2\pi \ag{Z}} (P_k(z \frac{\partial}{\partial z} + \bar{z} \frac{\partial}{\partial \bar{z}})f)(te^{i\theta}) e^{in\theta} \frac{d\theta}{2\pi} \\ &= \frac{(-1)^l}{n^l} \int_{\ag{R} / 2\pi \ag{Z}} (\left( z \frac{\partial}{\partial z} - \bar{z} \frac{\partial}{\partial \bar{z}} \right)^l P_k(z \frac{\partial}{\partial z} + \bar{z} \frac{\partial}{\partial \bar{z}})f)(te^{i\theta}) e^{in\theta} \frac{d\theta}{2\pi}. \end{align*} Hence, we deduce that \begin{align*} B_{\infty}^{k,\sigma}(f_n) &\leq \norm[n]^{-l} \left\{ \extNorm{(z\bar{z})^{\lfloor \frac{\sigma}{2} \rfloor}\left( z \frac{\partial}{\partial z} - \bar{z} \frac{\partial}{\partial \bar{z}} \right)^l P_k(z \frac{\partial}{\partial z} + \bar{z} \frac{\partial}{\partial \bar{z}})f}_{\infty} \right. \\ &\quad \left. + \extNorm{(z\bar{z})^{\lceil \frac{\sigma}{2} \rceil}\left( z \frac{\partial}{\partial z} - \bar{z} \frac{\partial}{\partial \bar{z}} \right)^l P_k(z \frac{\partial}{\partial z} + \bar{z} \frac{\partial}{\partial \bar{z}})f}_{\infty} \right\}. \end{align*} The right hand side is obviously bounded by some Schwartz norm of $f$.

nodes.name: Support and invariance indices
nodes.statement: Let $d \geq 1$ be an integer. For any $\Phi \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbf{F}^d)$ we define its \emph{support index} $D(\Phi) \in \ag{Z}$, \emph{additive invariance index} $\delta(\Phi) \in \ag{Z}$ and \emph{multiplicative invariance index} $m(\Phi) \in \ag{N}$ as follows. \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] $D(\Phi)$ is the largest integer $D$ such that $$ \Phi(\vec{x}) \neq 0 \Rightarrow \vec{x} \in \mathfrak{p}^D \times \cdots \times \mathfrak{p}^D. $$ \item[(2)] $\delta(\Phi)$ is the smallest integer $\delta$ such that $$ \Phi(\vec{x}+\vec{t}) = \Phi(\vec{x}), \forall \vec{x} \in \mathbf{F}^d, \vec{t} \in \mathfrak{p}^{\delta} \times \cdots \times \mathfrak{p}^{\delta}. $$ \item[(3)] $m(\Phi)$ is the smallest integer $m \geq 0$ such that for any $\kappa \in {\rm GL}_d(\mathfrak{o})$ with $\kappa-1 \in {\rm M}_d(\mathfrak{p}^m)$ $$ {\rm R}(\kappa).\Phi(\vec{x}) = \Phi(\vec{x}.\kappa) = \Phi(\vec{x}), \forall \vec{x} \in \mathbf{F}^d. $$ \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Defines for $p$-adic Schwartz functions the support index $D$, additive invariance index $\delta$ and multiplicative invariance index $m$.

nodes.name: Relations between the indices
nodes.statement: The three indices satisfy the following relations. \begin{itemize} \item[(0)] $m(\Phi) \leq \delta(\Phi)-D(\Phi)$. \item[(1)] For any $\kappa \in {\rm GL}_d(\mathfrak{o})$, we have $D({\rm R}(\kappa).\Phi)=D(\Phi)$, $\delta({\rm R}(\kappa).\Phi)=\delta(\Phi)$ and $m({\rm R}(\kappa).\Phi)=m(\Phi)$. \item[(2)] Let $\Four{\cdot}$ denote the Fourier transform $$ \Four{\Phi}(\vec{x}) = \int_{\mathbf{F}^d} \Phi(\vec{y}) \psi(-\vec{y}.\vec{x}) d\vec{y}. $$ Then we have $$ D(\Phi)+\delta(\Four{\Phi}) = \delta(\Phi) + D(\Four{\Phi}) = -\mathfrak{c}(\psi). $$ \item[(3)] More generally, let $I = \{ i_1, \cdots, i_j \} \subset \{ 1, \dots, d \}$. We define the partial Fourier transform $\Four[I]{\cdot} = \Four[i_1]{\Four[i_2]{ \cdots \Four[i_j]{\cdot}}}$. Then we have $$ \delta(\Four[I]{\Phi})) \leq \max(\delta(\Phi), -\mathfrak{c}(\psi)-D(\Phi)); $$ $$ D(\Four[I]{\Phi}) \geq \min(D(\Phi), -\mathfrak{c}(\psi)-\delta(\Phi)). $$ \end{itemize}
conclusions: $m(\Phi) \leq \delta(\Phi)-D(\Phi)$
$$ D(\Phi)+\delta(\Four{\Phi}) = \delta(\Phi) + D(\Four{\Phi}) = -\mathfrak{c}(\psi). $$
nodes.statement_short: $m\le\delta-D$; the indices are $GL_d(\mathfrak o)$-invariant; Fourier transform swaps $D$ and $\delta$ up to the conductor of $\psi$.
nodes.label: DdmRel

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.17
nodes.statement:
(0) and (1) are obvious from definition. (3) follows easily from (2). We prove (2) as follows. From $$ \Four{\Phi}(\vec{x}+\vec{t}) = \int_{\mathfrak{p}^{D(\Phi)} 	imes \cdots 	imes \mathfrak{p}^{D(\Phi)}} \Phi(\vec{y}) \psi(-\vec{y}.\vec{x}) \psi(-\vec{y}.\vec{t}) d\vec{y}, $$ we see that for $\vec{t} \in \mathfrak{p}^{-\mathfrak{c}(\psi)-D(\Phi)}$, $\vec{y}.\vec{t} \in \mathfrak{p}^{-\mathfrak{c}(\psi)}$ hence $\psi(-\vec{y}.\vec{t})=1$ and $\Four{\Phi}(\vec{x}+\vec{t}) = \Four{\Phi}(\vec{x})$. Thus $$ \delta(\Four{\Phi}) \leq -\mathfrak{c}(\psi)-D(\Phi). $$ On the other hand, if $\vec{x} 
otin \mathfrak{p}^{-\mathfrak{c}(\psi)-\delta(\Phi)} 	imes \cdots 	imes \mathfrak{p}^{-\mathfrak{c}(\psi)-\delta(\Phi)}$ then at least for one component, say $x_1 
otin \mathfrak{p}^{-\mathfrak{c}(\psi)-\delta(\Phi)}$, i.e., $v(x_1) < -\mathfrak{c}(\psi)-\delta(\Phi)$. As $t_1$ runs under the condition $v(t_1)=-\mathfrak{c}(\psi)-1-v(x_1) \geq \delta(\Phi)$, $x_1t_1$ runs under the condition $v(x_1t_1)=-\mathfrak{c}(\psi)-1$. Hence at least for one $t_1$, $\psi(x_1t_1) 
eq 1$. Writing $\vec{t}=(t_1,0,\dots,0)$, we get $$ \Four{\Phi}(\vec{x}) = \int_{\mathbf{F}^d} \Phi(\vec{y}+\vec{t}) \psi(-\vec{y}.\vec{x}) d\vec{y} = \int_{\mathbf{F}^d} \Phi(\vec{y}) \psi(-\vec{y}.\vec{x}) d\vec{y} \cdot \psi(\vec{t}.\vec{x}) = \psi(t_1x_1) \Four{\Phi}(\vec{x}). $$ Hence $\Four{\Phi}(\vec{x}) = 0$ and $$ D(\Four{\Phi}) \geq -\mathfrak{c}(\psi)-\delta(\Phi). $$ Replacing $\Phi$ with $\Four{\Phi}$ in the above argument gives the inequalities in the opposite direction.
nodes.statement_short: (0),(1) from definitions, (3) from (2); (2) by checking invariance and support of $\mathfrak F\Phi$ through character orthogonality.

nodes.name: Weighted semi-norms on p-adic Schwartz space
nodes.statement:
For $l \in [1,\infty]$, $\vec{\sigma} \in \ag{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, we put the semi-norm $\mathcal{S}_l^{\vec{\sigma}}$ on $\mathcal{S}(\mathbf{F}^d)$ by $$ \mathcal{S}_l^{\vec{\sigma}}(\Phi) = \extNorm{ 
orm[\vec{x}^{\vec{\sigma}}]_{\mathbf{F}} \cdot \Phi }_l. $$ Here we have written:  egin{itemize} \item $\Norm_l$ is the ${m L}^l$-norm on $\mathbf{F}^d$. \item For $\vec{x}=(x_i)_{1 \leq i \leq d} \in \mathbf{F}^d, \vec{\sigma}=(\sigma_i)_{1 \leq i \leq d} \in \ag{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, $
orm[\vec{x}^{\vec{\sigma}}]_{\mathbf{F}}=\Pi_{i=1}^d

nodes.name: Norm relations via indices
nodes.statement: We have the following relations of norms for any $\Phi \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbf{F}^d)$. \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] $\Norm[\Phi]_{\infty} \leq q^{\frac{d\delta(\Phi)}{l}} \Norm[\Phi]_l$ and $\Norm[\Phi]_l \leq q^{-\frac{dD(\Phi)}{l}} \Norm[\Phi]_{\infty}$. \item[(2)] $\mathcal{S}_l^{\vec{\sigma}}(\Phi) \leq q^{-\norm[\vec{\sigma}] D(\Phi)} \Norm[\Phi]_l$. \end{itemize}
conclusions: $\Norm[\Phi]_{\infty} \leq q^{\frac{d\delta(\Phi)}{l}} \Norm[\Phi]_l$ and $\Norm[\Phi]_l \leq q^{-\frac{dD(\Phi)}{l}} \Norm[\Phi]_{\infty}$
$\mathcal{S}_l^{\vec{\sigma}}(\Phi) \leq q^{-\norm[\vec{\sigma}] D(\Phi)} \Norm[\Phi]_l$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.19
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $d=1$; average over a ball of invariance for the first, bound by the support volume for the others.

nodes.name: Space B_c(Z; varpi)
nodes.statement: For any $c \in \ag{R}$, we define ${\rm B}_c(\ag{Z};\varpi)$ to be the space of functions $f: \varpi^{\ag{Z}} \to \ag{C}$ satisfying \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] $\lim_{n \to -\infty} f(\varpi^n) q^{-n\sigma} = 0$ for any $\sigma > 0$. \item[(2)] $\lim_{n \to +\infty} f(\varpi^n) q^{-n \sigma} = 0$ for any $\sigma > c$. \end{itemize} The subspace ${\rm B}_c^0(\ag{Z};\varpi) \subset {\rm B}_c(\ag{Z};\varpi)$ is defined by replacing (1) with \begin{itemize} \item[(1')] $f(\varpi^n)=0$ for $n \ll -1$. \end{itemize}

nodes.name: Space H_c(C; q)
nodes.statement: For any $c \in \ag{R}$ we define ${\rm H}_c(\ag{C};q)$ to be the space of meromorphic functions $M: \ag{C} \to \ag{C}$ satisfying \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] $M(s+i\frac{2\pi}{\log q}) = M(s)$ for all $s \in \ag{C}$. \item[(2)] $M(s)$ is holomorphic for $\Re s > c$. \end{itemize}

nodes.name: Semi-norms B_l^sigma
Semi-norms H_l^sigma
Independence of B-topology from l, p-adic
nodes.statement: The topology on ${\rm B}_c(\ag{Z};\varpi)$ defined by $B_l^*$ does not depend on $l$. More precisely, for any $f \in {\rm B}_c(\ag{Z};\varpi)$ we have for $1 \leq l < \infty$ and $\epsilon > 0$ small with $\sigma - \epsilon > c$ $$ B_l^{\sigma}(f) \ll_{\epsilon,l} B_{\infty}^{\sigma-\epsilon}(f) + B_{\infty}^{\sigma+\epsilon}(f); $$ $$ B_{\infty}^{\sigma}(f) \leq B_l^{\sigma}(f). $$
conclusions: The topology on ${\rm B}_c(\ag{Z};\varpi)$ defined by $B_l^*$ does not depend on $l$.
nodes.label: BEquiv

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.24
nodes.statement: The first follows from $$ B_l^{\sigma}(f)^l \leq B_{\infty}^{\sigma-\epsilon}(f) \sum_{n \geq 0} q^{-n\epsilon} + B_{\infty}^{\sigma+\epsilon}(f) \sum_{n < 0} q^{n\epsilon}. $$ The second is obvious by positivity.
nodes.statement_short: Split the sum at $n=0$; the reverse inequality by positivity.

nodes.name: Independence of H-topology from l, p-adic
nodes.statement: The topology on ${\rm H}_c(\ag{C};q)$ defined by $H_l^*$ does not depend on $l$. More precisely, for any $M \in {\rm H}_c(\ag{C};q)$ we have for $1 \leq l < \infty$ and $\epsilon > 0$ small with $\sigma - \epsilon > c$ $$ H_l^{\sigma}(M) \leq H_{\infty}^{\sigma}(M); $$ $$ H_{\infty}^{\sigma}(M) \ll_{\epsilon} H_l^{\sigma-\epsilon}(M) + H_l^{\sigma+\epsilon}(M). $$
conclusions: The topology on ${\rm H}_c(\ag{C};q)$ defined by $H_l^*$ does not depend on $l$.
nodes.label: HEquiv

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.25
nodes.statement: The first is obvious. For the second, let $s_0$ be any complex number with $\Re s_0 = \sigma$ and $0 < \Im s_0 < 2\pi / \log q$. Selecting the contour joining $\sigma+\epsilon$, $\sigma+\epsilon + i 2\pi / \log q$, $\sigma - \epsilon + i 2\pi / \log q$ and $\sigma-\epsilon$, we see $$ \log q \cdot M(s_0) = \int_0^{\frac{2\pi}{\log q}} \frac{M(\sigma+\epsilon+i\tau)}{\sigma+\epsilon+i\tau - s_0} \frac{\log q d\tau}{2\pi} - \int_0^{\frac{2\pi}{\log q}} \frac{M(\sigma-\epsilon+i\tau)}{\sigma-\epsilon+i\tau - s_0} \frac{\log q d\tau}{2\pi}. $$ Using H\"older inequality we deduce \begin{align*} \log q \cdot \norm[M(s_0)] &\leq \frac{1}{\epsilon} H_l^{\sigma+\epsilon}(M) \cdot \left( \int_0^{\frac{2\pi}{\log q}} \frac{\log q d\tau}{2\pi} \right)^{\frac{l-1}{l}} + \frac{1}{\epsilon} H_l^{\sigma-\epsilon}(M) \cdot \left( \int_0^{\frac{2\pi}{\log q}} \frac{\log q d\tau}{2\pi} \right)^{\frac{l-1}{l}} \\ &= \frac{1}{\epsilon} H_l^{\sigma+\epsilon}(M) + \frac{1}{\epsilon} H_l^{\sigma-\epsilon}(M). \end{align*} We conclude by taking $\sup$ with respect to $\Re s_0 = \sigma$.
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy's formula on a rectangular period contour, then Hölder.

nodes.name: Continuity of p-adic Mellin transform and inverse
nodes.statement: The two maps $$ {\rm B}_c(\ag{Z};\varpi) \to {\rm H}_c(\ag{C};q), f \mapsto \Mellin{f}(s) = \sum_{n \in \ag{Z}} f(\varpi^n) q^{-ns}, \text{ for } \Re s > c; $$ $$ {\rm H}_c(\ag{C};q) \to {\rm B}_c(\ag{Z};\varpi), M \mapsto f_M(\varpi^n) = \int_0^{\frac{2\pi}{\log q}} M(\sigma+i\tau) q^{n(\sigma + i \tau)} \frac{\log q d\tau}{2\pi}, \forall \sigma > c $$ are continuous with respect to the above topologies defined by semi-norms.
conclusions: are continuous with respect to the above topologies defined by semi-norms.
nodes.label: BHEquiv

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.26
nodes.statement: The continuity follows from $$ H_{\infty}^{\sigma}(\Mellin{f}) \leq \sum_{n \in \ag{Z}} \norm[f(\varpi^n)] q^{-n\sigma} = B_1^{\sigma}(f); $$ $$ B_{\infty}^{\sigma}(f_M) \leq \sup_{n \in \ag{Z}} \int_0^{\frac{2\pi}{\log q}} \norm[M(\sigma+i\tau) q^{n i \tau}] \frac{\log q d\tau}{2\pi} = H_1^{\sigma}(M). $$
nodes.statement_short: Direct $L^1$-$L^\infty$ estimates of the Mellin pair.

nodes.name: Angular components on varpi^Z
nodes.statement:
Note that the abstract part of Definition \ref{FourF^1} still makes sense in the current case, i.e., for any function $f: \mathbf{F} \to \ag{C}$ and $\xi \in \widehat{\mathbf{F}^1}$ we can define
	$$ f_{\xi}(\varpi^n) = \int_{\mathbf{F}^1} f(\varpi^n u) \xi(u) du, n \in \ag{Z}. $$

nodes.name: Angular components of p-adic Schwartz functions
nodes.statement: For any $f \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbf{F})$, $f_{\xi} \neq 0$ only for $\xi$ satisfying $\mathfrak{c}(\xi) \leq m(f)$, hence for only finitely many $\xi$. We have $f_{\xi} \in B_0^0(\ag{Z};\varpi)$ and $$ B_{\infty}^{\sigma}(f_{\xi}) \leq \mathcal{S}_{\infty}^{\sigma}(f), \forall \sigma > 0. $$
conclusions: $f_{\xi} \neq 0$ only for $\xi$ satisfying $\mathfrak{c}(\xi) \leq m(f)$, hence for only finitely many $\xi$
We have $f_{\xi} \in B_0^0(\ag{Z};\varpi)$

For any $\Phi \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbf{F}^2)$, let $$ D = \min(D(\Phi), -\mathfrak{c}(\psi)-\delta(\Phi)); \delta = \max(\delta(\Phi), \mathfrak{c}(\psi)-D(\Phi)). $$ Then for any $\sigma > 
orm[\Re s]$ and $\epsilon > 0$ with $\sigma - \epsilon >

The first part is a direct consequence of the previous lemma and the following inequalities deduced from Proposition ef{DdmRel} and ef{SchEquiv}: $$ D(\Four[2]{{m R}(\kappa).\Phi}) \geq \min(D(\Phi), -\mathfrak{c}(\psi)-\delta(\Phi)) = D; $$ $$ m(\Four[2]{{m R}(\kappa).\Phi}) \leq \delta(\Four[2]{{m R}(\kappa).\Phi}) - D(\Four[2]{{m R}(\kappa).\Phi}) \leq \delta - D; $$ $$ \extNorm{\Four[2]{{m R}(\kappa).\Phi}}_{\infty} \leq q^{\delta(\Four[2]{{m R}(\kappa).\Phi})} \extNorm{\Four[2]{{m R}(\kappa).\Phi}}_2 \leq q^{\delta} \Norm[\Phi]_2. $$ The ``moreover'' part follows from a direct computation (or \cite[Theorem 4.6.5]{Bu98}) $$ W_{\Phi}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};a(\varpi^n)) = q^{- rac{n}{2}}  rac{\alpha^{n+1}- eta^{n+1}}{\alpha -  eta} 1_{n \geq 0}, 	ext{ with } \alpha = \xi(\varpi)q^{-s},  eta=\omega\xi^{-1}(\varpi) q^s, $$ which implies for $n \geq 1$ $$

nodes.statement:
Writing $D_v=\min(D(\Phi_v), -\mathfrak{c}(\psi_v)-\delta(\Phi_v))$ for $v<\infty$, it follows from Proposition ef{LocWhiBdA} and ef{LocWhiBdNA} that for any $\epsilon > 0$ and $N \gg 1$
	$$ \extnorm{W_{\Phi}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};na(y)\kappa)} \ll_{\epsilon,N,\Phi} \prod_{v \mid \infty} \min(

	The bound is uniform when $\Re s$ lies in a fixed compact interval. Together with Lemma ef{GTechEst}, we obtain
